title: Windows automation probe — WIN20's WinUI 3 plane witness
note: WIN20's own probe window, not the product. Kept as a surface because it is what proves the automation plane works at all, and because its two SecondaryCommands are the recorded unoracled pair: a CommandBar's overflow items are not realised while the overflow is closed, so they exist on neither the control view nor the raw view.

title: Windows Settings board
note:
Seven sections, measured on the automation plane rather than counted in the markup: settings.section.router, .harnesses, .sessionanalyst, .updates, .security, .ambientsurface, .advanced, each publishing a name. Three of them carry a switch; the other four carry WIN13's governance prose because this build has no harness settings, no session analyst and no update check. The switches publish as Button carrying TogglePattern - which is what a WinUI ToggleSwitch is on the plane, and what made DEF-076's first reading say there were none.

SINCE DEF-087 ONE OF THE THREE REACHES THE MACHINE AND TWO ARE DISABLED. `Launch router daemon at sign-in` registers and removes WIN23's logon task, and the board seeds it from the Windows task scheduler rather than from its own memory; the state persists to %APPDATA%\MCPRouter\shell-settings.json. `Show status in notification area` places and removes a real notification-area icon (DEF-101), registered by GUID so that something other than this application can ask the shell whether it is there. `Confirm before removing a server` - narrowed from `Require confirmation on destructive operations`, which named a class of operations this build does not have - decides whether the Servers board asks before it sends the router the one destructive verb the shell speaks (DEF-102). Both were DISABLED with a reason until those two landed, and neither is any more: nothing on this board now moves a boolean that reaches nothing. `Copy the loopback endpoint` copies (DEF-088). The two disabled switches still publish a readable toggle state, so the census rows over them are unchanged.

title: Windows Discover detail dialog
note: WIN7's detail dialog, addressable since DEF-075's fix: every x:Named element carries an AutomationProperties.AutomationId, and the containers that publish no text of their own carry a Name. The text elements deliberately do not - a TextBlock's own Text IS its accessible name and a static Name would overwrite it, so the controls listed here are ids. Opened by shell-lane.ps1 section 3b, which needs the registry search to return a store row first; where it does not, that census row reads `unoracled` rather than passing.
